text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed sharply higher following sharp gains in New York. March added $25 to close at $1,650 per tonne, while May closed $24 higher at $1,667. The sharp rise in prices makes the market vulnerable to technical reactions and funds could be tempted to take profits.

Arabica futures in New York closed sharply higher following a state- sector strike in Colombia which entered its second day. A senior official said coffee shipments to the ports had been adversely affected although he was not able to give an exact figure. Road freight has dropped by 30 per cent as fear of leftist guerilla attacks and disruption by striking workers has kept many trucks off the roads. Julian Parra, commercial director of the Colombian Transport Federation said traditional products such as flowers and coffee were among the most affected, but added the situation was beginning to get back to normal.
March closed 8.30 cents/lb higher at 171.85 cents/lb, while May gained 5.65 cents/lb to close at 163.20 cents/lb.

HONDURAS - According to the Honduran Coffee Institute export revenues in 1996/97 could reach $360 million, up from $300 million the previous year. Export revenues will be higher in 1996/97 inspite of a lower crop than last season due to higher world coffee prices. Coffee production in 1996/97 (October/September) is forecast to fall to below 2 million 60- kg bags, down from 2.3 million bags harvested in 1995/96.

POLAND - Poland imported 152,944 bags of coffee in August 1996, 9 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.093 million bags, nearly 7 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose to 1.536 million bags from 1.442 million bags the previous year. The main suppliers of green coffee in January/August 1996 were Ivory Coast (129,800 vs 137,100 bags), India (127,600 vs 66,500 bags), Indonesia (219,700 vs 120,200 bags) and Vietnam (143,400 vs 190,600 bags).
